clue.text: Unduly led astray by star for so long

indicators.note: something gone astray has wandered off its proper course, so these letters leave their order

parts.note: unduly means excessively, too much
the letters of led rearranged
a pip is the star on an army officer's shoulder

explanation.surface: Someone excessively misled by a celebrity for a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like part of the surface's time phrase, but it is the definition. TOODLE-PIP is dated British slang for goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual farewells, ways of saying goodbye to someone leaving.

clue.text: Right in grip of hard depression

indicators.note: to be in the grip of something is to be held inside it

parts.note: hard and tough are synonyms
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone tightly held by a severe depression, perhaps an economic slump.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a low point or hollow, a depression in land or in a graph of the economy.

clue.text: One restricted by guns regulation

indicators.note: something restricted by others is hemmed in on both sides by them

parts.note: ordnance is artillery, big guns
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person limited by gun regulations, as in a gun-control law.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an official rule or decree, a regulation laid down by an authority.

clue.text: Vindaloo and rice prepared for a famous painter

indicators.note: food that is prepared is chopped and mixed, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters of all three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A curry dinner cooked up for a celebrated artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renaissance master who painted the Mona Lisa is among the most celebrated artists in history.

clue.text: Seabird's lost in gust

indicators.note: when something is lost it is gone, so the following short word drops out

parts.note: the puffin is a seabird with a bright bill
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A seabird has gone missing in a blast of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition placing the bird in the wind, but it is the pair of letters the seabird loses.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a short burst of wind or breath, which is what a gust is.

clue.text: Pedestrianise, to make progress easier?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: lay paving stones along a road for walkers
second meaning: the idiom for preparing things so that something can follow smoothly

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the first meaning is a whimsical, literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to prepare conditions for something; literally, laying a paved route lets walkers go easily.

clue.text: Drank regularly round base

indicators.note: to turn round is to face the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol habitually, as a toper does

explanation.surface: Someone drinking steadily around a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like the signal to take alternate letters, but it belongs to the definition of tope, which means to drink habitually.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a headquarters or storage station, a base for troops, vehicles or supplies.

clue.text: Ambiguous, like Sackville-West?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... remark carries two meanings at once
second meaning: a hyphenated surname made of two family names, like that of writer Vita Sackville-West

explanation.walkthrough: Vita Sackville-West was an English writer and gardener; British hyphenated surnames are called double-barrelled, after a gun with two barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-barrelled gun fires two ways at once, hence a statement with two senses or a two-part hyphenated surname.

clue.text: Suggest a tip

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to indicate or hint at
second meaning: the sharp end of a pencil or needle

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as offering advice, a tip for a punter; 'tip' here is the sharp end of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to indicate or imply, and the noun names the sharp end of an object.

clue.text: Abstemious count after support

indicators.note: one thing placed after another follows it, setting the order of the two parts

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball
a total is a count or sum

explanation.surface: A sober aristocrat placed second behind someone backing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman, but here it is the sum of a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person never drinks alcohol, the most complete kind of moderation in drinking.

clue.text: It's more than likely this'll give you a good run for your money

definitions.text: It's more than likely this'll give you a good run for your money

parts.words: It's more than likely this'll give you a good run for your money
parts.note: surface reading: something very probable that offers fair value or a stiff challenge

parts.words: a good run for your money
parts.note: setter's reading: a racehorse priced shorter than evens, expected to run well for those who back it

explanation.walkthrough: 'A good run for your money' is an idiom for a strong contest, but here it is literal: a horse you bet on running well. 'More than likely' hints at odds better than even.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner priced at odds-on is judged more likely to win than lose, so backing it promises a good run.

clue.text: Sympathetic cheering

definitions.meaning: first meaning: friendly and kindly in manner
second meaning: pleasantly warm or enlivening

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests supportive applause, but 'cheering' is an adjective meaning pleasant and enlivening.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a warm, friendly person and also mild, cheerful conditions such as sunshine.

clue.text: Knife fight about cash register with one pound missing

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it on all sides

parts.note: a set-to is a brief scrap or fight

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so that letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a till is a shop's cash register
L is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A knife fight breaks out over a shop till, with a pound gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: A cleansing process alien to Serbians

indicators.note: something alien is strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar shape

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some form of cleaning that people from Serbia find foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: Abstersion is a rare formal word for wiping or washing clean, from the Latin for wipe away.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstersion is the act of cleansing or purging, the same idea as a cleansing process.

clue.text: Lie in bed, poorly, not fit enough to eat

indicators.note: something poorly made is in bad shape, so these letters are put into another form

parts.note: the letters of all three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick person staying in bed, too unwell to manage a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' reads as British for ill, describing the patient, but it signals the rearrangement; 'not fit enough' then describes food, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Inedible food is unsuitable for eating, whether spoilt, poisonous or simply unpalatable.

clue.text: The pair answer a South African politician

parts.note: both means the two of them, the pair
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Two people respond to an official from South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: P. W. Botha was South Africa's prime minister and then state president in the apartheid era.
explanation.definitionFit: Botha is the surname of apartheid-era South African leaders, including P. W. Botha and Pik Botha.

clue.text: Teacher confused about one mass, a peninsula

indicators.note: to be about something is to be wrapped around it
a confused thing is muddled, so the letters of the first word are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of teacher rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A muddled schoolteacher talking about one religious mass on a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimea is a peninsula jutting into the Black Sea from southern Ukraine.

clue.text: Teacher courted a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters fall into a different order

parts.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher wooed someone who proved a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disaster' reads as a noun describing the courted person, but it signals the rearrangement of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is someone who instructs others, a more formal word for a teacher.

clue.text: Father embracing sapper, 22

definitions.note: refers to the answer to 22-across, a noun meaning fear

indicators.note: to embrace someone is to wrap one's arms around them, holding them inside

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
sappers are military engineers, and RE stands for the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A dad hugging a military engineer, cross-referenced to another answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 refers to the answer at 22-across, which means great fear. The Royal Engineers are the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread and terror are synonyms: both name intense fear of something about to happen.

clue.text: A setter barking round end of rose bushes

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, holding it inside
barking is British slang for mad, so the letters of the words before it go haywire

parts.note: the letters of both words, rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of rose

explanation.surface: A setter dog yapping as it runs around some rose bushes.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter is a gundog, so 'barking' seems literal; it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea trees are shrubs of Australia and New Zealand, the source of tea tree oil, so they are bushes.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink, make unknown

parts.note: a brand or make is a product's trade name
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A drink whose brand nobody recognises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning brand, as in a make of car.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Spelunkers sheltering notice corpses

indicators.note: to shelter something is to keep it protected inside

parts.note: spelunkers are people who explore caves
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: Cave explorers taking cover, then spotting dead bodies underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: a small advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadavers are dead human bodies, especially those used for dissection, so they are corpses.

clue.text: Boring type starts to discuss weatherman's early evening broadcast

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, the only ones kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A dull person begins talking about the TV weather forecaster's evening bulletin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dweeb is slang for a dull, socially awkward person, a nerd or bore.

clue.text: Troublesome child, last to admit mistake

indicators.note: the last belonging to a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of admit
an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A naughty child who is always the final one to own up to a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admit' looks like the verb of confessing, and 'last to' a phrase about being slowest; together they mean the last letter of admit.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is an informal name for a badly behaved, mischievous child.

clue.text: Cream plectrum?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the best of a group
second meaning: a small flat piece used to strum a guitar

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' suggests the dairy product, but it means the elite, the best.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream and the pick both mean the finest selection, and a guitar plectrum is commonly called a pick.

clue.text: Two articles about unseen spymaster in film

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the two short words go outside the rest

parts.note: the definite article and an indefinite article
invisible means unable to be seen
M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A pair of reports concerning a hidden head of espionage in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper stories, but they are grammatical articles, one definite and one indefinite, split so they wrap around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Invisible Man is the 1933 film, and later versions, based on the H. G. Wells novel.

clue.text: Poor performer spending time with teacher

indicators.note: spending something means using it up, so it is no longer there

parts.note: a rabbit is British sporting slang for a weak player, especially a poor batsman in cricket
T is the abbreviation for time, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A weak student or player spending time with their tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sporting slang a rabbit is a hopeless player, particularly a tail-end batsman in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious leader; the Hebrew word itself means my master or teacher.

clue.text: Orchid exposed by peeress

parts.note: naked means uncovered, exposed
a peeress is a woman of noble rank, titled Lady

explanation.surface: A rare flower revealed by a noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: A peeress is a woman holding a British noble title, addressed as Lady.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked lady is a common name for several flowers, including an orchid whose pale petals resemble a small figure.
